correctness.rationale: Subtracting the two petal ODEs forces equality at every equilibrium, and all positive petals have the same amplitude. The hub balance gives an iff scalar cubic whose exact maximum yields the fold thresholds and complete labeled count. Inactive petals have an eigenvalue -1+lambda*h=y/(1-y)>0. In full-support states the Jacobian splits into negative antisymmetric and zero-sum modes plus a 2x2 block with trace negative and determinant m*lambda^2*y^3-2, whose sign changes at the cubic peak; zero has Jacobian -I. A standalone reproduction script passed 5 symbolic checks, 34 exact-rational checks/identities, 88 parameter cases and 536 nonzero state-residual evaluations. No inference from finite experiments to the infinite theorem is needed.

value.rationale: The exact count resolves a natural structural question for a sparse, strongly clustered, hub-mediated higher-order contact motif and exposes exponential proliferation of stationary states despite only two locally exponentially stable equilibria. Critical rate thresholds distinguish activation on k versus k+1 petals, with an \(m^{-1/3}\) onset law. This is an all-size, all-rate classification including physically meaningful boundary states, not a routine restatement of the known homogeneous scalar fold, nor a small numerical improvement.
